name: Rajma Masala
steps: Pick over dry kidney beans, rinse, and soak in plenty of water for 8–12 hours. Drain and rinse again; soaking is additional to the listed cooking time.
Cover the soaked beans with fresh water and boil vigorously for at least 30 minutes. Continue cooking until completely soft, adding water as needed; never use raw or undercooked kidney beans.
Check several beans by pressing with a spoon: they should mash easily, with no firm or chalky centre. Keep the cooked beans and their cooking liquid aside while making the gravy.
Finely chop the tomatoes. Heat oil in a separate pan, add cumin and let it sizzle, then add tomatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes until thick and pulpy, stirring the base often.
Lower the heat and add coriander powder, turmeric and chilli powder. Stir briefly, using a splash of bean cooking liquid if the spices catch, then add the fully cooked beans.
Add enough cooking liquid for a spoonable gravy and stir in salt. Simmer gently for about 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken the sauce.
Taste and adjust the consistency with more cooking liquid if needed. The gravy should cling to the tender beans; rest briefly off the heat and serve with your chosen meal.
tips: Do not cook raw kidney beans only in a low-temperature slow cooker.
substitutions: For a cream finish, plain whisked curd may work: cool the pan and add gradually. Recheck dietary filters before substituting.
passiveTime: Allow additional soaking, resting, chilling or fermentation as specified in the steps.
